Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings: Sudden-onset, painless left arm paralysis with left facial tingling, dysphagia, and dysarthria on awakening; symptoms persistent and possibly worsening. Vascular risk factors: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, age, former smoking. Lives alone.  
- Working diagnosis: Suspected acute stroke (ischemic etiology likely, right MCA territory), consistent with transcript and DDx.  
- Supporting DDx and reasoning:
  - Acute ischemic stroke (right MCA territory) – High likelihood: Focal neurologic deficits (left arm paralysis, dysarthria, dysphagia, left facial sensory change) with vascular risk factors and persistent deficits.
  - Intracerebral hemorrhage – Medium likelihood: Abrupt focal deficits in hypertensive older adult; cannot be distinguished clinically without imaging.
  - TIA – Low likelihood: Deficits ongoing >1 hour and worsening.  
- Plan per transcript: Emergency ambulance arranged for transfer to local ED/A&E; ED to contact stroke specialist for urgent assessment and potential acute treatment; patient advised to unlock front door and wait in hallway; clinician remained on the line until ambulance arrival.

- Acute ischemic stroke (right MCA territory) – High: Sudden focal deficits (left arm paralysis, dysarthria/dysphagia, facial tingling) with vascular risk factors; persistent symptoms.  
- Intracerebral hemorrhage – Medium: Abrupt focal deficits in hypertensive older adult; indistinguishable from ischemic stroke without imaging.  
- Transient ischemic attack (TIA) – Low: Symptoms ongoing >1 hour and possibly worsening.
